class.name: TimerInfo
class.brief_description: A shareable description of a timer.

members.member: Times at which [signal Timer.alert_reached] is emitted, once per run. The times are in shown time: the time left for a countdown (for example [code]10.0[/code] for "10 seconds left"), the elapsed time for a stopwatch.
A free text describing the timer. It is not used by the engine.
If [code]true[/code], the timer ignores [member Engine.time_scale] and updates with the real elapsed time.
If [code]true[/code], the timer restarts when it reaches [member total_time]. The remainder of the frame carries over. On a [Timer] node this is the opposite of [member Timer.one_shot].
Specifies when the timer is updated during the main loop.
Specifies whether the timer keeps running while the [SceneTree] is paused. [b]Note:[/b] This is ignored by [Timer] nodes, which follow [member Node.process_mode].
The interval in seconds between [signal Timer.ticked] signals. [code]0[/code] disables ticks.
Whether the timer counts down or up.
The speed of this timer relative to its clock. [code]2.0[/code] runs twice as fast, [code]0.0[/code] freezes it.
The name of the timer, used by [method TimerServer.get_timer]. If empty, a [Timer] node uses its node name.
The time in seconds the timer takes to end. For a stopwatch, [code]0[/code] means it has no end. On a [Timer] node a value greater than [code]0[/code] replaces [member Timer.wait_time].

constants.constant: The timer counts down from [member total_time] to [code]0[/code]. The shown time is the time left.
The timer counts up from [code]0[/code]. The shown time is the elapsed time. If [member total_time] is greater than [code]0[/code], the timer ends there.
The timer stops while the [SceneTree] is paused.
The timer keeps running while the [SceneTree] is paused.
Update the timer every process (rendered) frame.
Update the timer every physics process frame.
